events.text: Zhansaya Abdumalik born 12 January 2000
events.subject: self
events.quote: born 12 January 2000

events.text: She won her first trophy at a national tournament.
events.subject: self
events.quote: in January 2007 she won her first trophy at a national tournament

events.text: She won the girls U8 section at the Asian Youth Chess Championship.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2008 , she won the girls U8 section at both the Asian Youth Chess Championship , held in Tehran , and the World Youth Chess Championships

events.text: She won the girls U8 section at the World Youth Chess Championships.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2008 , she won the girls U8 section at both the Asian Youth Chess Championship , held in Tehran , and the World Youth Chess Championships

events.text: She shared 1st–2nd places in the girls U10 division at the 2010 World Youth Championships, taking the silver medal on tiebreak.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In the 2010 World Youth Championships in Porto Carras , she shared 1st–2nd places in the girls U10 division , taking the silver medal on tiebreak

events.text: She was awarded the Woman International Master (WIM) title.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2011 , she was awarded the Woman International Master (WIM) title

events.text: She won the girls U12 title at the World Youth Championships.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Later that same year , Zhansaya won the girls U12 title at the World Youth Championships held in Caldas Novas , Brazil

events.text: She finished as runner-up in the World Junior Girls Chess Championship.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In September 2013 , she finished as runner-up in the World Junior Girls Chess Championship

events.text: She was voted the best girl under-20 player of 2013 at the 1st Annual Asian Chess Excellence Awards.
events.subject: self
events.quote: she was voted the best girl under-20 player of 2013 at the 1st Annual Asian Chess Excellence Awards , held in June 2014

events.text: She won the Brno Open in the Czech Republic, scoring 7½/9 points.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In November 2013 , she won the Brno Open in the Czech Republic scoring 7½/9 points

events.text: She won the bronze medal in the Asian Womens Blitz Championship of 2014.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Zhansaya won the bronze medal in the Asian Womens Blitz Championship of 2014

events.text: She won the bronze medal at the 2015 World Junior Girls Championship.
events.subject: self
events.quote: She won the bronze medal also at the 2015 World Junior Girls Championship in Khanty-Mansiysk

events.text: She won the womens championship of Kazakhstan.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2016 , she won the womens championship of Kazakhstan

events.text: She won the 6th Krystyna Hołuj-Radzikowska Memorial in Wrocław, Poland.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2016 , she won the womens championship of Kazakhstan and the 6th Krystyna Hołuj-Radzikowska Memorial in Wrocław , Poland

events.text: She won the team bronze medal at the 2016 Asian Nations Cup.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In the 2016 Asian Nations Cup she won the team bronze medal and an individual silver playing board two

events.text: She won an individual silver playing board two at the 2016 Asian Nations Cup.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In the 2016 Asian Nations Cup she won the team bronze medal and an individual silver playing board two

events.text: She earned her first GM norm with a score of 7/9 at the World Open.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In July 2017 , Abdumalik earned her first GM norm with a score of 7/9 at the World Open

events.text: She moved to the ASEAN Chess Academy in Singapore, where she trained with GM Zhang Zhong.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2012 , she moved to the ASEAN Chess Academy in Singapore where she trained with GM Zhang Zhong

events.text: The Zhansaya Abdumalik Chess Academy was opened in Almaty.
events.subject: part_of_self
events.quote: In January 2014 , Anatoly Karpov visited Almaty to open the newly established Zhansaya Abdumalik Chess Academy

events.text: Karpov and Abdumalik played a four-game match after the ceremony; Abdumalik won one blitz game and the second one was drawn.
events.subject: self
events.quote: after the ceremony . Karpov won both rapid games ( 20 minutes per player ) , while Abdumalik won one blitz game and the second one was drawn

dropped.text: She earned a final GM norm at the Karpos Open in March.
dropped.subject: self
dropped.quote: she earned her final two GM norms in succession at the Karpos Open in March

dropped.text: She earned a final GM norm at the Budapest Spring Festival in April.
dropped.subject: self
